A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OUP/COUP research. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, and appendices support comparison, including the new Appendix D in v2.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A/C report original OUP/COUP runtime evaluations, comparisons with UP and a naive procedure, and analyses of doubling conditions and exploration schedules.

after.justification: v2 retains original OUP/COUP evaluations and adds comparisons with five other configurators, including results across five seeds in Section 5.3 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same sampling, confidence bounds, selection, termination, and captime-doubling procedures. The improved doubling condition already appears in v1. v2's algorithm walkthroughs explain existing steps.

E1.justification: Both versions use minisat, cplex_rcw, and cplex_region for SAT, wildlife-conservation, and combinatorial-auction configuration experiments. The log-Laplace and uniform utility families are retained; the additional comparisons introduce no new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: Section 5.3 adds evaluated comparisons with Successive Halving, Hyperband, AC-Band, ImpatientCapsAndRuns, and Structured Procrastination with Confidence. These substantially expand v1's comparisons with UP, the naive procedure, and OUP/COUP; AC-Band is evaluated with both log-Laplace and default objectives.

E3.justification: The new comparison measures percentage gap to the best configuration against CPU time. Its runtime setup uses uniform-utility caps of 100 for minisat and 3000 for CPLEX, quantile-capped evaluation with quantile parameters 0.1 and 0.2, and baseline-specific budget/cap grids. These supplement the retained experiments rather than replace their settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds a quantile-parameter robustness comparison: Figure 8 uses 0.2 versus Figure 5's 0.1. Section 5.3 and Appendix D also examine baseline parameter sensitivity and AC-Band's objective choice. The existing doubling-condition and exploration-schedule analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 provides no empirical seed counts or uncertainty regions. v2's new comparison reports averages over five seeds and minimum–maximum error regions in Figure 5, introducing substantial variability reporting. This does not establish an increased run count for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Figures 5 and 8 add extensive percentage-gap results. Section 5.3 reports OUP/COUP eventually identifying the best configuration for every seed, Hyperband finding good RCW configurations earlier but retaining a gap, and weak AC-Band performance under log-Laplace utility. Retained runtime curves also change, notably Figure 3, without a stated method change.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–2, Lemmas 1–5, Theorems 1–2, and Appendix B's proofs retain the same mathematics. Appendix A's doubling-condition derivation is also retained. The added phase-sampling explanation restates Algorithm 2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and scientific conclusion retain the same contributions: utilitarian configuration over infinite spaces, anytime near-optimality guarantees, and improved finite-space performance over UP. The additional comparative evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly discusses comparisons across different objectives and guarantees, interpreting anytime refinement as avoiding sensitivity to fixed budget choices. Appendix D connects AC-Band's default metric to its racing mechanism. Existing limitations concerning benchmark breadth and choosing utility functions remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix D documents baseline budgets, cap grids, Hyperband multipliers, ICAR parameters, and SPC settings. It also describes correcting AC-Band's CPLEX cap from 900 to 10000 seconds. Section 5 newly discloses an environment where restarting runs is impossible; both versions retain the anonymous-repo-link placeholder.

R1.justification: v2 adds Jamieson and Talwalkar (2016) and Li et al. (2018), and expands discussion of Successive Halving, Hyperband, and previously cited configurators with different guarantees. The established bandit and utilitarian research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 adds walkthroughs in Sections 3–4, Section 5.3, and Appendix D, and refines algorithm terminology. It removes the generic societal-impact closing passage. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds a six-panel comparison figure and a three-panel robustness figure with uncertainty displays. Retained plots receive revised axes, legends, and panel labeling; old Figures 5–6 become Figures 6–7. Title, author, heading, and page formatting also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical support primarily compares against UP and a naive baseline. Section 5.3 and Appendix D address this important gap through five additional configurators, explicit evaluation choices, five-seed variability, and detailed settings, substantially strengthening evidence of practical competitiveness while retaining the theory. Different objectives still limit direct comparisons, and code access remains a placeholder, but the gain in evidence and transparency is substantial.
